hook: A supplement bottle says "500 mg of calcium per tablet." A lab can check that claim with a balance: dissolve the tablet, measure how much calcium it holds and compare with the pure compound. The same idea, measuring one element to judge a whole mixture, is how chemists test the purity of medicines, metals and food.

prereq.q: What is the mass percent of oxygen in water, H₂O (molar mass 18.02 g/mol)?

options: Two or more elements joined in a fixed ratio
Two substances stirred together in any ratio
Any substance that is a gas
prereq.why: A compound has its elements in a fixed ratio, which gives it a fixed composition.

figure.caption: Classifying matter: a pure substance has one kind of particle and a fixed composition; a mixture has more than one kind, in proportions that can vary.

chain.cause: A pure substance contains one kind of particle
chain.effect: its composition is fixed, the same in every sample

chain.cause: A mixture contains two or more substances that are not bonded into one kind of particle
chain.effect: its proportions can vary from sample to sample

chain.cause: Each pure compound has a known mass percent of each element
chain.effect: measuring one element in a sample shows how much of that compound it holds

chain.cause: Comparing that amount with the sample's mass
chain.effect: gives the purity, as long as no other part of the mixture holds the same element

ideas: A mixture holds two or more substances in proportions that can vary. A homogeneous mixture is uniform throughout; a heterogeneous mixture is not.
In a particulate diagram, a pure substance shows one kind of particle; a mixture shows more than one. What you see and measure in bulk is the macroscopic level.
Elemental analysis: measure the mass of one element, convert it to the compound with the compound's mass percent.
Purity = mass of the wanted compound ÷ mass of the sample × 100.

misconception.wrong: Anything that contains two or more elements is a mixture.
misconception.right: Compounds also contain two or more elements, joined in a fixed ratio into one kind of particle. A mixture has more than one kind of particle, and its proportions can vary.

summary: Pure substances have one kind of particle and a fixed composition; mixtures have more than one, in variable proportions, and can be homogeneous or heterogeneous. Elemental analysis measures one element in a sample and uses the pure compound's mass percent to find how much of the compound is present, giving its purity.
